index.description: ChameLab: desktop, mobile and web app for ChameleonUltra and ChameleonLite, with firmware and a command line client.
index.hero.1: Built for ChameleonUltra & ChameleonLite
index.hero.3: Desktop, mobile and web app for ChameleonUltra and ChameleonLite, together with an extended firmware and the command line client.
index.device-card.3: One device. All your cards.
index.app.2:
Everything your device can do.
In one place.
index.app.3: One app for Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and the browser. USB on desktop and in the browser, Bluetooth on phones, TCP everywhere.
index.app.5: All eight slots at a glance, with each card's name and LED color. Drag to reorder, tap to activate, edit HF and LF separately.
index.app.7: One LF slot holds up to eight LF cards of any emulated type, in any mix, and sends the next one each time the reader's field appears — one steady card per tap — so you can walk through them until the right card opens. No other Chameleon firmware or app can do this.
index.app.9: ISO14443-A and LF scans. MIFARE Classic Mini, 1K and 4K dumps with your key dictionaries, edited as hex and emulated in one tap.
index.app.11: A card library with search and color tags. Imports ChameleonUltraGUI, Proxmark3, Flipper .nfc/.rfid, MCT, .bin and .eml.
index.app.13: Write LF IDs to T55xx and MIFARE Classic to Gen1a / Gen2 magic cards.
index.app.15: Gen1a / Gen2 modes, write modes, nonce detection for mfkey32, Ultralight / NTAG version, signature and counters.
index.app.17: LED animation, button actions, long-press threshold, sleep timeout, BLE pairing, factory reset and firmware updates over USB or Bluetooth.
index.app.19: Record a reader talking to the card in the active slot, every frame labelled, with MIFARE Classic keys recovered on the spot. Capture the 125 kHz signal as a zoomable waveform and decode it.
index.app.21: Every long operation (dumps, key recovery attacks, writing magic cards, sniffing) has a Stop button and leaves the device ready for the next one. In ChameleonUltraGUI many of them can only be waited out.
index.app.22: The web version needs Chrome or Edge on a desktop: Firefox and Safari do not support Web Serial.
index.why.3: How the app compares with the Flutter ChameleonUltraGUI and the command line client.
index.why.4.aria-label: Feature comparison, scroll horizontally on small screens
index.why.10: Runs in the browser, nothing to install
index.why.11: Multi-card LF: up to 8 LF cards of any type in one slot
index.why.22: One codebase, five targets. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and WebAssembly share the same views and protocol code, so a fix lands everywhere at once.
index.why.23: The firmware moves with the app. Features like slot colors are added on both sides together and shipped in the same release.
index.why.24: Adaptive layout. Side navigation on a desktop, a drawer on a phone, and the keyboard and system Back button handled properly on Android.
index.why.25: Cards first. Read a card, save it to the library, put it into any slot, and the slot shows which saved card it holds, matched by UID.
index.why.26: Still on the roadmap: QR sharing.
index.firmware.3: The ChameLab firmware runs on both ChameleonUltra and ChameleonLite. Here is what is new in it.
index.firmware.5: An LF slot can hold up to eight cards of any emulated LF type (EM410x, Electra, HID Prox, ioProx, Viking, PAC, Jablotron, IDTECK, Pyramid), mixed in any order. Each time the reader's field appears the slot sends the next card in the list, one steady card per tap, wrapping back to the first — so you tap until the right card opens. Neither the stock firmware nor any other app or firmware for the Chameleon can do this.
index.firmware.6: One card per tap: a single steady card per field appearance is the cleanest transition for access readers, and there is no per-card timing to tune.
index.firmware.7: Position kept across sleep: the next card is remembered between taps; a battery pull or switching slots restarts at the first card.
index.firmware.8: Kept with the slot: the list survives restarts and follows the slot when slots are swapped. Single-card slots work as before.
index.firmware.9: Build the list in the ChameLab slot editor from your saved cards and drag to reorder. Apps use the commands 5907–5909; the details are in LF card cycling.
index.firmware.11: Each card in a slot can have its own LED color, so you can tell which card is active by looking at the device. The RGB lines are driven by PWM, so any color works, not only the seven primary mixes. A slot that holds both an HF and an LF card alternates between their two colors. Slots without a color keep the familiar HF / LF colors.
index.firmware.12.aria-label: Example: eight slots with their own colors; slot 3 holds HF and LF cards
index.firmware.13: Pick a color in the ChameLab slot editor, or from the CLI: hw slot color -s 3 --hf -c FF5722, --default goes back to the standard color. Apps use the new DATA_CMD_SET_SLOT_COLOR (1900) and DATA_CMD_GET_ALL_SLOT_COLORS (1901) commands.
index.firmware.15: No more full flash after slot switching Fix: flash records stayed open after reading, so they could never be garbage-collected. After enough slot switches, saving failed until a reboot.
index.firmware.17: The ChameLab app on desktop, Android and iOS updates the firmware for you: it offers the newest release for your device and flashes it over USB or Bluetooth. To flash by hand:
index.firmware.18: Download ultra-dfu-app-<version>.zip or lite-dfu-app-<version>.zip from the release below. The -full packages also contain the bootloader and are only needed for recovery.
index.firmware.19: Put the device into DFU mode: hw dfu in the CLI, or hold button B while plugging in USB.
index.firmware.20: Flash the package with firmware/flash-dfu-app.sh, nRF Connect for mobile or nRF Connect for Desktop.
index.firmware.21: Slots, cards and settings are kept by an application update. See the full changelog.

guide.description: Step-by-step guide to ChameLab: connect a ChameleonUltra or ChameleonLite, read and save cards, emulate them in slots, use multi-card LF, dictionaries and sniffing.
guide.guide-hero.3: From plugging in your ChameleonUltra or ChameleonLite to reading a card, recovering its keys and emulating it. The screenshots are from the Windows app; macOS, Linux, Android and the web app look and work the same way.
guide.connect.3: Download ChameLab for your platform from the downloads, or open the web app in Chrome or Edge on a desktop. Plug the Chameleon in over USB. It shows up under Detected devices on its own: select it and press Connect.
guide.connect.4.alt: The Connect page with one Chameleon detected on COM8 and a Connect button
guide.connect.5: The Connect page lists every Chameleon plugged in over USB.
guide.connect.6: USB works on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android (with an OTG cable) and in the web app.
guide.connect.7: Bluetooth is used on phones and tablets. If pairing with a PIN is enabled on the device, enter the PIN when the phone asks for it.
guide.connect.8: Network bridge (TCP) connects to a host:port bridge or simulator. Expand it under the device list.
guide.connect.9: You don't need a device for the card library, dictionaries and app settings. They work offline, and so does opening saved sniff captures.
guide.device.3: Once you're connected, Connect in the sidebar is replaced by Chameleon. This page shows everything about the device at a glance:
guide.device.5: Operating mode: Emulator presents the active slot to readers as a card, Reader lets the device read cards placed on it.
guide.device.6: Active slot: tap a number to switch slots, or use the arrows. Filled slots are drawn in their LED color, and the line below shows the HF and LF cards in the active slot.
guide.device.7: Hardware and firmware identity: model, firmware and git version, chip ID and BLE address, each with a copy button.
guide.device.8.alt: The Chameleon page showing battery at 99 percent, Emulator mode, slot 1 active with Office door on HF and three LF cards
guide.device.9: Slot 1 is active: a MIFARE Classic card on HF and three LF cards that take turns.
guide.device.11: The Firmware update card checks for the newest ChameLab firmware and installs it over USB or Bluetooth. Your slots, cards and settings are kept. Install from file… flashes a DFU package you downloaded yourself.
guide.device.13: Scroll down for the settings stored on the device: LED animation, sleep timeout, what buttons A and B do on a short and a long press, the long-press threshold, and Bluetooth pairing with a PIN. Clear bonded devices forgets paired phones; Reset to defaults and Factory reset are at the very bottom.
guide.device.14.alt: Device settings: LED animation, sleep timeout, button actions, long-press threshold, Bluetooth pairing and PIN
guide.device.15: Button A on a long press is set to read a card and emulate its UID.
guide.cards.3: Cards is your library of saved cards. Group them into folders (New folder, or the folder icon in the sidebar), search by name, type or UID, and filter by HF or LF. Each card has a color, which also becomes its slot LED color.
guide.cards.4: Select a card to open it in the editor. From there you can change its details and memory, Duplicate or Export it, Assign to slot to emulate it, or Write it to a blank: LF IDs to T55xx, MIFARE Classic to Gen1a / Gen2 magic cards.
guide.cards.5.alt: The Office folder with three cards; the Office door MIFARE Classic 1K card is open in the editor with its memory map
guide.cards.6: A MIFARE Classic 1K card in the editor. The grid shows the state of each sector; the hex view below shows the selected sector.
guide.cards.8: Press + Add card and choose how:
guide.cards.9: Scan HF or Scan LF: hold a card on the Chameleon and read it (see Read a card). For LF, pick the protocol below first.
guide.cards.10: Import file: ChameleonUltraGUI and Proxmark3 JSON, Flipper .nfc / .rfid, MCT, .bin and .eml dumps.
guide.cards.11: Enter manually: pick a type and type the UID or ID.
guide.cards.12.alt: The Add card panel with Scan HF, Scan LF, Import file and Enter manually
guide.cards.13: Four ways to add a card.
guide.read.3: Place the card on the Chameleon and press + Add card → Scan HF. ChameLab shows the type, UID, SAK, ATQA and ATS straight away.
guide.read.4: For a MIFARE Classic card the memory isn't read yet. Press Try keys to try every key from your dictionaries, plus the built-in defaults, on every sector.
guide.read.5: If some sectors stay red (No key), press Check recovery methods. ChameLab tests the card and offers the attacks that work on it.
guide.read.6: When every sector is green, press Save card to keep the full dump in your library.
guide.read.7.alt: A freshly scanned MIFARE Classic 1K card with UID 4D 4F 4E 53 and an unread memory map
guide.read.8: Right after the scan: identity known, memory not read yet.
guide.read.9.alt: Dictionary check in progress: sectors marked red have no key, with a Stop button
guide.read.10: Trying dictionary keys. Red sectors have no matching key, blue is the sector being searched.
guide.read.12: The memory header shows what ChameLab found out about the card, here PRNG Static (fixed nonces), and the toolbar offers the attacks that fit: darkside, nested, static nested, static encrypted nested or hardnested. To sniff keys from a reader with mfkey32 instead, load the card into a slot first. Recovered keys are saved under the card's UID in Known card keys, so the next read of the same card is instant.
guide.read.13.alt: Recovery methods offered for the card: Static nested enabled, others disabled
guide.read.14: This card has a static PRNG, so Static nested is offered.
guide.read.15.alt: All 16 of 16 sectors read and shown in green, with Save card at the bottom
guide.read.16: About fifteen seconds later: 16 of 16 sectors read. Save the card to keep the dump.
guide.read.17: Every long operation, from dictionary checks to attacks, writing magic cards and sniffing, has a Stop button. Stopping keeps the keys and blocks already found, and the device is ready for the next job.
guide.slots.3: The Chameleon has eight slots. Each slot holds one HF card and one LF card, and the active slot is what readers see. Slots shows all eight at once. Select a slot to edit it on the right.
guide.slots.4: Select a slot and press Choose saved under HF or LF.
guide.slots.5: Pick a card from your library. Search works here too.
guide.slots.6: Adjust the emulator options if you need to: LED color, Gen1a / Gen2 magic mode, write mode and PRNG type for MIFARE Classic; magic mode and password detection for Ultralight / NTAG.
guide.slots.7: Press Save. ChameLab writes the slot to the device and keeps it after a reboot. If you switch slots with unsaved changes, it asks first.
guide.slots.8.alt: Choosing a saved HF card for slot 1 from a list of three cards
guide.slots.9: Choosing an HF card for slot 1. Only cards of the right frequency are listed.
guide.slots.10.alt: Emulation slots page with slots 1 to 3 filled and slot 1 open in the editor with MIFARE Classic emulator options
guide.slots.11: Three slots in use. Slot 1 is open with its MIFARE Classic emulator options.
guide.slots.12: Switch the active slot on the Chameleon page, or with the device buttons. With the default settings, button A goes to the next slot and button B to the previous one.
guide.multi-lf.3: One LF slot can hold up to eight LF cards of any emulated type, in any mix: EM410x, Electra, HID Prox, ioProx, Viking, PAC, Jablotron, IDTECK and Pyramid. Each time the reader's field appears, the slot sends the next card in the list. Tap again and again until the right card opens the door.
guide.multi-lf.4: Select a slot and add the first card with Choose saved under LF.
guide.multi-lf.5: Press Add saved for each additional card. The counter shows how many of the eight places are taken.
guide.multi-lf.6: Drag the cards to change the order, then Save.
guide.multi-lf.7.alt: The LF section of slot 1 holding three EM410x cards: Parking gate, Server room and Garage, 3 of 8
guide.multi-lf.8: Three LF cards in one slot. The device sends one per tap, then starts again from the first.
guide.multi-lf.9: The position in the list is kept while the device sleeps. Removing the battery or switching slots starts again at the first card. More details: LF card cycling.
guide.dictionaries.3: Dictionaries are lists of MIFARE Classic keys that Try keys uses when reading a card. Create one with + New dictionary or Import a .dic file. In the editor, type one key per row: an empty row at the end adds a key, and pasting a list adds them all at once. Repeated keys and rows you have changed are highlighted.
guide.dictionaries.4: Known card keys at the top holds every key ChameLab has recovered, sorted by card UID. You don't need to add them anywhere: they are tried automatically on the card they came from.
guide.dictionaries.5.alt: Key dictionaries page with Common defaults and Office keys; Common defaults open showing twelve keys
guide.dictionaries.6: Two dictionaries; Common defaults is open in the editor.
guide.tools.3: Tools shows what goes over the air between readers and cards.
guide.tools.4: Sniff HF: the Chameleon answers a reader as the card in its active slot and records both sides. Every frame is labelled, and MIFARE Classic keys are recovered from the reader's authentications on the spot. Choose how long to listen, press Capture and hold the Chameleon to the reader. Traces load and save as Proxmark3 .trace files.
guide.tools.5: Sniff LF: records 32 ms of the 125 kHz antenna signal with a tag held on the antenna. You get a zoomable waveform, a level summary, a guess at the modulation and clock, and a Manchester decode. Captures save as raw .bin and open later without a device.
guide.tools.6.alt: Tools page with Sniff HF and Sniff LF
guide.tools.7: Pick a sniffer to open it.
guide.settings.3: Settings holds the settings of the app itself. They apply right away and work without a device: accent color, scan sounds (a beep when a scan finishes, a buzz when no card is found) and the update check.
guide.settings.4: Export backup saves all your cards and key dictionaries to one file, and Import backup restores it, for example on another computer or phone.
guide.settings.5.alt: Settings page with accent color, scan sounds, backup and version
guide.settings.6: App settings. The Chameleon's own settings are on the Chameleon page.
guide.settings.7: Questions or problems? Open an issue on GitHub.
